cim_eredeti: My favorite third-party Windows screenshotting tool just got even better at extracting text from images
szoveg_eredeti:
I may be a huge Linux fanboy now, but back when I used Windows, ShareX was my weapon of choice for taking screenshots. In fact, it's one of the apps I really miss from the Windows side of things.

As such, it's always good to see ShareX still getting updates, and the newest one is fantastic news for people who use it to extract text from images. ShareX 22.5.0 replaces the Windows-based Optical Character Recognition (OCR) with a new tool based on PaddleOCR.

As announced on the ShareX website (via Neowin), the development team has released version 22.5.0 of the popular screenshotting software. The highlight for this version is an upgrade to its OCR tool:

Replaced Windows OCR with AI powered PaddleOCR, which gives significantly more accurate results. It supports over 100 languages out of the box, with no language packs to download and no switching between languages, and everything still runs locally on your device.

Clicking on the link within that quote takes you to the PaddleOCR GitHub page, and honestly, it looks pretty great from the demos there. It seems it can handle both handwritten and tightly packed written English quite well, and that's just one of the 100+ languages it supports.

Of course, version 22.5.0 isn't just about OCR. There are some really nice tweaks in here, too. The image editor is getting a handful of new options to play with, such as "Right-click deletes the shape under the cursor" and "Size window to fit image." Plus, opening the region capture tool happens about twice as fast now, which is great to hear, as that was my most-used tool of the lot. There's even a pixel art editor now, which comes with "layers, an animation timeline, tilemaps, slices, and sprite sheet import and export."
